claim: Russia made agreement by the de facto authorities a condition of its own support for the appointment. The Council text requests consultation but does not condition appointment on that agreement.
The African members expected an envoy to support the existing mission’s work. The adopted text separately preserves the mandate and work of UNAMA.
The Council requires agreement from the de facto authorities before the Secretary-General can appoint the envoy.
The Secretary-General appointed the envoy without the authorities’ agreement, so Russia then withheld its support.
Russia said it would support the appointment as long as consultation with the de facto authorities occurred, even without their agreement.
The Council requested the envoy for the stated purpose of complementing UNAMA’s work.
The adopted text transferred UNAMA’s role to the Special Envoy, as the African members had proposed.
Speaking for the African members, Ghana attributed its support specifically to paragraph 3’s full safeguard for the mandate and work of the Special Representative.
